speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly how long you've had the fever and wrist pain, and when did you first notice these skin lesions?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the appearance of the skin lesions and tell me if they are itchy or painful? Do you have any other joints that are currently hurting?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the violaceous lesions and your recent trip to Minnesota, could these be tick bites, and do you recall seeing a rash on your trunk or feeling numbness? I would like to examine your wrist more closely and check for any other systemic signs.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall seeing a "bullseye" rash on your trunk or any tick bites during your camping trip? REQUEST TEST: Erythema migrans serology and Lyme PCR.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: The requested tests (Erythema migrans serology and Lyme PCR) are not available in the current data. Available findings indicate: WBC 15,000/μL (elevated); Joint Aspiration (Left Wrist) WBC >50,000/μL with Gram-negative diplococci; STI Screen Positive for Gonorrhea.

speaker: Doctor
text: The joint aspiration showing Gram-negative diplococci combined with your positive STI screen confirms the source of your infection. Given your sexual history and these specific lab findings, I can now confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection
